blocks.source: Vol III, Trajectory Curation, § Fallacies and Pitfalls
blocks.md: A data collection pipeline can preserve every execution record faithfully and still assemble a counterproductive training set. The mistakes below stem from confusing raw trace telemetry with the deliberate pedagogical choices required to train an agent, and each carries tangible computational or behavioral costs.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Recovery demonstrations matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: A policy trained only on clean prefixes meets off-path states it never saw, so recovery demonstrations keep the mistake as conditioning context and select only the assessed correction as the target.

questions.q: The section **Fallacies and Pitfalls** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: With k attempts per task a random trace split puts most tasks on both sides, so partitions are assigned to task groups that hold every attempt, paraphrase, fork, and derived record.
A policy trained only on clean prefixes meets off-path states it never saw, so recovery demonstrations keep the mistake as conditioning context and select only the assessed correction as the target.
One recorded run can yield imitation material, a preference comparison, or a rollout fixture, and each use has its own admission conditions rather than inheriting the run's outcome.

A failure earns a weight update only if it persists with complete context, a well-formed interface, and a healthy runtime, so counterfactual probes run up the intervention ladder from context and schema to SFT and then RL.
